items.pronunciation_notes: The flap ढ़ is released with breath, and the vowel before -ना drops: paṛhnaa in two syllables.

learn.explanation_en: पढ़ना means to read, and also to study, so a student पढ़ता है whether or not a book is open. Its stem is पढ़. You met the word in Module 2 as the example for the breathy flap ढ़, which is the tongue flicking forward with a puff of air after it — not a stop.

examples.note: The thing read comes before the verb.
पत्र keeps its final vowel after a conjunct in र.
The two halves of literacy, as a fixed pair.

practice.question: पढ़ना
practice.explanation_en: पढ़ना is to read, and by extension to study. लिखना is to write.

game.question_en: पढ़ना — which part is the stem, once -ना is removed?
game.explanation_en: Removing -ना leaves पढ़, which keeps the dot and is the stem.

items.pronunciation_notes: The two न letters run together and the n is held longer than a single one: sunnaa.

learn.explanation_en: सुनना covers both hearing and listening, so it does the work of two English verbs. Its stem is सुन. The written word has two न letters in a row and the vowel between them drops, so the n is genuinely held longer, in the same way as the doubled consonants from Module 3.

examples.note: गाना is both a song and the verb to sing.
आवाज़ carries the dotted ज़ and is feminine.
The same verb for deliberate listening.

practice.question: सुनना
practice.explanation_en: सुनना is to hear or to listen. बोलना is to speak.

game.question_en: सुनना — which part is the stem, once -ना is removed?
game.explanation_en: Removing -ना leaves सुन with a single न, which is the stem.

items.pronunciation_notes: The vowel before -ना drops but the middle one stays, giving samajhnaa — the medial schwa case from Module 3.

learn.explanation_en: समझना means to understand, and its stem is समझ. This is the exact word Module 3 used to show that medial schwa deletion is variable: समझ keeps its middle vowel while समझना drops the one before the ending. The झ is voiced and breathy at once, so keep the murmur going rather than saying j and then h.

examples.note: The language comes before the verb.
बात is feminine despite its consonant ending.
The two halves of using a language.

practice.question: समझना
practice.explanation_en: समझना is to understand. समझाना, with a longer vowel, is to explain.

game.question_en: समझना — which part is the stem, once -ना is removed?
game.explanation_en: Removing -ना leaves समझ, said with its middle vowel intact: samajh.

summary.recap_en: This level added पढ़ना, सुनना and समझना — the verbs for taking language in. Each hides a stem: पढ़, सुन and समझ.
summary.next_up_en: Next: लेना, देना and बनाना, three verbs with very short stems.

items.pronunciation_notes: A clear l and a flat ए with no glide: lenaa, two syllables.

learn.explanation_en: लेना means to take, and its stem is ले. It pairs with देना, to give, and the two turn up together constantly. Much later they take on a second job as helpers attached to other verbs, changing the shade of meaning rather than adding one of their own — but that belongs to a far later module.

examples.note: The thing taken comes before the verb.
The same pattern with another object.
A fixed pair, used as a phrase.

practice.question: लेना
practice.explanation_en: लेना is to take. देना is to give.

game.question_en: लेना — which part is the stem, once -ना is removed?
game.explanation_en: Removing -ना leaves ले, a single syllable, which is the stem.

items.pronunciation_notes: Dental द with the tongue on the teeth, and a flat ए: denaa.

learn.explanation_en: देना means to give, and its stem is दे. Keep the द dental, with the tongue against the teeth — pulled back it drifts towards ड and the word stops being recognisable. Like लेना it later doubles as a helper verb, and the two are usually taught as a pair for that reason.

examples.note: The thing given comes before the verb.
You will hear this offered constantly.
The same pattern again.

practice.question: देना
practice.explanation_en: देना is to give. लेना is to take.

game.question_en: देना — which part is the stem, once -ना is removed?
game.explanation_en: Removing -ना leaves दे, which is the stem.

items.pronunciation_notes: Three syllables, banaanaa, with the middle vowel long and the first one short.

learn.explanation_en: बनाना means to make or to build, and its stem is बना. It is the everyday verb for cooking — खाना बनाना is how you say to cook, literally 'to make food'. Note the vowel lengths: the first is short and the second long, so it is ba-naa-naa and not baa-na-naa.

examples.note: The ordinary way to say cooking.
The same verb for preparing a drink.
And for building something too.

practice.question: बनाना
practice.explanation_en: बनाना is to make or build. With खाना it is the ordinary word for cooking.

game.question_en: बनाना — which part is the stem, once -ना is removed?
game.explanation_en: Removing -ना leaves बना, which is the stem.

summary.recap_en: This level covered लेना, देना and बनाना. लेना and देना have the shortest stems you will meet — ले and दे — and both take on a second life as helper verbs much later.

items.pronunciation_notes: The vowel before -ना drops, so the word is rahnaa in two syllables, and र is a single tap.

learn.explanation_en: रहना covers living somewhere, staying somewhere and remaining in a state, so it stretches across several English verbs. Its stem is रह. Remember that र is a single tap of the tongue rather than the English curl, and that the vowel before the ending drops.

examples.note: यहाँ carries the crescent from Module 3.
The same verb for remaining in a state.
A very common thing to wish someone.

practice.question: रहना
practice.explanation_en: रहना is to live or to stay. It also covers remaining in a state.

game.question_en: रहना — which part is the stem, once -ना is removed?
game.explanation_en: Removing -ना leaves रह, which is the stem.

items.pronunciation_notes: Unaspirated क with no puff of air, and the vowel before -ना drops: kahnaa.

learn.explanation_en: कहना means to say or to tell, and its stem is कह. It overlaps with बोलना but is not identical: बोलना leans towards the act of speaking, while कहना leans towards the words said. Keep the opening क free of breath — with a puff it becomes ख, a different letter.

examples.note: The thing said comes before the verb.
धीरे never changes form.
The two sides of a conversation.

practice.question: कहना
practice.explanation_en: कहना is to say or tell. बोलना leans more towards the act of speaking.

game.question_en: कहना — which part is the stem, once -ना is removed?
game.explanation_en: Removing -ना leaves कह, which is the stem.

items.pronunciation_notes: Light unaspirated च with no puff, and the vowel before -ना drops: chalnaa.
items.gloss_en: to walk, to move, to go along

learn.explanation_en: चलना means to walk, but it stretches much further: machines चलते हैं when they run, and चल on its own is the everyday 'come on, let's go'. Its stem is चल. You met the word in Module 2 as one half of the चल and छल pair, so keep the opening sound free of breath.

examples.note: धीरे is an adverb and never changes.
तेज़ carries the dotted ज़.
Used when setting off together.

practice.question: चलना
practice.explanation_en: चलना is to walk or move. It also covers machines running.

game.question_en: चलना — which part is the stem, once -ना is removed?
game.explanation_en: Removing -ना leaves चल, which is also the everyday word for 'come on'.

summary.recap_en: This level added रहना, कहना and चलना. All three drop the vowel before the ending, so their stems are रह, कह and चल.
summary.next_up_en: Next: सोना, उठना and बैठना finish the twenty verbs.

items.pronunciation_notes: A flat ओ with no w-glide at the end: sonaa, two syllables.

learn.explanation_en: सोना means to sleep, and its stem is सो. It is also the noun for gold, exactly as खाना is both food and to eat — two unrelated words that happen to share a spelling, with only the sentence to tell them apart. You met it in Module 1 as an example of the flat ओ, so keep the vowel steady with no w at the end.

examples.note: यहाँ carries the crescent.
कम never changes form.
The pair that covers a day's ends.

practice.question: सोना
practice.explanation_en: सोना is to sleep. The same spelling is also the noun for gold.

game.question_en: सोना — which part is the stem, once -ना is removed?
game.explanation_en: Removing -ना leaves सो, which is the stem.

items.pronunciation_notes: The retroflex ठ is released with breath, and the vowel before -ना drops: uṭhnaa.

learn.explanation_en: उठना means to get up, whether from a chair or from bed, and its stem is उठ. The ठ is an aspirated retroflex, so the tongue curls back and a puff of air follows — do not reach for the th of English 'think', which does not exist in Hindi. You met the word in Module 2 while learning the short उ.

examples.english: to get up in the morning
examples.note: सुबह ends with a light ह that colours the vowel.
धीरे never changes form.
Two retroflex verbs as a pair.

practice.question: उठना
practice.explanation_en: उठना is to get up or rise. बैठना is to sit down.

game.question_en: उठना — which part is the stem, once -ना is removed?
game.explanation_en: Removing -ना leaves उठ, which is the stem.

items.pronunciation_notes: The open ऐ, then an aspirated retroflex ठ, and the vowel before -ना drops: baiṭhnaa.

learn.explanation_en: बैठना means to sit or to sit down, and its stem is बैठ. It packs together two things English speakers find awkward: the open ऐ, which is a single vowel close to the a of 'cat' rather than the 'eye' its transliteration suggests, and the aspirated retroflex ठ. Take them one at a time.

examples.note: A very common invitation.
The pair from the last card, reversed.

practice.question: बैठना
practice.explanation_en: बैठना is to sit down. उठना is to get up.

game.question_en: बैठना — which part is the stem, once -ना is removed?
game.explanation_en: Removing -ना leaves बैठ, which is the stem.

summary.recap_en: This level completed the twenty verbs with सोना, उठना and बैठना. Every one of the twenty is named by an infinitive in -ना, and stripping that ending always gives the stem.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the common adjectives, starting with the three you have already seen in dozens of examples.

items.pronunciation_notes: The flap ड़ — the tongue curls back and flicks forward once — then a long final vowel: baṛaa.

learn.explanation_en: बड़ा means big or large, and it also means elder when applied to people, so बड़ा भाई is an elder brother rather than a large one. It ends in -ा, so it inflects: बड़ा, बड़ी, बड़े. You have seen all three forms in examples throughout this module without being told what they were.

examples.note: घर is masculine singular, so -ा.
बहन is feminine, so -ी — and the meaning shifts to age.
Masculine plural, so -े.

practice.question: बड़ा
practice.explanation_en: बड़ा is big or large. Applied to a person it means elder.

game.question_en: ___ घर — which form of बड़ा fits?
game.explanation_en: घर is masculine and singular, so बड़ा keeps its -ा form.

items.pronunciation_notes: Aspirated छ with a clear puff of air, then a retroflex ट: chhoṭaa.

learn.explanation_en: छोटा is the opposite of बड़ा in both senses: small in size, and younger when used of people. It ends in -ा and inflects the same way. Keep the opening sound aspirated — a clear puff of air — since without it the word drifts towards चोटा, which is not a word but sounds wrong immediately.

examples.note: भाई is masculine, so -ा, and the meaning is about age.
बहन is feminine, so -ी.
Masculine plural, so -े.

practice.question: छोटा
practice.explanation_en: छोटा is small. Applied to a person it means younger.

game.question_en: ___ बहन — which form of छोटा fits?
game.explanation_en: बहन is feminine, so छोटा becomes छोटी.

items.pronunciation_notes: The च्छ stack runs a plain च into an aspirated छ, so the second half carries the puff of air: achchhaa.

learn.explanation_en: अच्छा means good, and on its own it is also the all-purpose acknowledgement of Hindi conversation — 'right', 'I see', 'okay'. You will hear it constantly as a single word. It ends in -ा and inflects normally. The stack in the middle from Module 3 pairs a plain च with an aspirated छ, so only the second half gets the breath.

examples.note: खाना is masculine, so -ा.
किताब is feminine, so -ी.
Masculine plural, so -े.

practice.question: अच्छा
practice.explanation_en: अच्छा is good. On its own it also works as 'right' or 'I see'.

game.question_en: ___ चाय — which form of अच्छा fits?
game.explanation_en: चाय is feminine, so अच्छा becomes अच्छी.

summary.recap_en: This level began the adjectives with बड़ा, छोटा and अच्छा — three words that have appeared in examples since the first level of this module. All three end in -ा, so all three inflect three ways.
summary.next_up_en: Next: more adjectives, including several that never change form at all.
